clue.text: All good, by the sound of it

indicators.note: says the word for good is to be heard rather than spelt, giving a different spelling

parts.note: good in the saintly sense means holy

explanation.surface: Someone sums up a situation as entirely good, judging only by what they have heard.
explanation.walkthrough: HOLY said aloud is the same as WHOLLY.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb, all (as in 'all alone') means completely or entirely.

clue.text: Gadabout, much more honest in conversation?

indicators.note: words used in conversation are spoken, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: way is informal for much, as in 'way better'; fairer means more just or honest

explanation.surface: A restless traveller who is, when chatting, far more truthful than others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way fairer' is the informal phrase for much more honest.
explanation.definitionFit: A wayfarer is a traveller on foot, someone always on the move like a gadabout.

clue.text: Start — as film actor may appear?

definitions.meaning: the ... of something is its beginning
a film actor appears ..., where the scenes are shot

explanation.surface: Kick off, as a movie star might show up.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the beginning of something and, split in two, being present where filming happens.

clue.text: Cricket side supposedly gone to get drunk?

parts.note: leg side is the half of a cricket field behind the batsman's legs
less means without, so the leg side is supposedly gone

explanation.surface: A cricket team that has apparently vanished to go and get drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field divides into the leg side and the off side; here the leg side is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Legless is British slang for so drunk one cannot stand up.

clue.text: Man, for example, apprehended by coppers, only

indicators.note: a thing apprehended by these words is caught and held within their letters

explanation.surface: A man, perhaps a suspect, is arrested by police officers alone.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'copPERS ONly'. 'Man' looks like a fellow arrested, but it stands for mankind or any human.
explanation.definitionFit: A man, or indeed any human being, is an example of a person, an individual.

clue.text: Mission ending in failure, swimmer stuck in well!

indicators.note: the ending in a word is its final letter
something stuck in another is lodged within it

parts.note: my! and well! are both exclamations of surprise
a bass is a fish, a swimmer

explanation.surface: A task ends badly when a fish gets stuck down a well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well!' with its exclamation mark is the interjection, not a water shaft; the fish goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An embassy is a diplomatic mission, the body of envoys and their building abroad.

clue.text: As may be gum in fur that's loosened with grease

indicators.note: letters loosened from their places are free to rearrange

explanation.surface: Chewing gum caught in fur that is worked loose with grease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loosened' jumbles FUR and GREASE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewing gum is often sold without sugar, sweetened instead with substitutes.

clue.text: Put in order, men finally put away

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: to put away food is to eat it

explanation.surface: Order restored, the men were at last locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put away' looks like imprisonment, but it means consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: To neaten is to tidy, making things orderly.

clue.text: Faculty certainly entertained by cardinal

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is held inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: eight is a cardinal number, as opposed to an ordinal
certainly as an affirming reply is yes

explanation.surface: A university department is assuredly hosted by a churchman of high rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a prince of the Church, but here it is a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is one of the bodily senses, which are also called faculties.

clue.text: Fresh T-shirt on, collecting grotty little bits

indicators.note: a thing collecting another takes it inside
fresh means new, so the letters are given a new order

parts.note: grotty is British slang for unwell, ill

explanation.surface: Putting on a clean T-shirt that picks up shabby little bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' rearranges T-SHIRT ON into TRIONTHS, and ILL goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trillionth is a minute fraction, so trillionths are very tiny portions.

clue.text: One supposedly can't choose goods in cart

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: to cart something is to carry it, to bear it
G is short for good, so two goods give two Gs

explanation.surface: Someone is unable to pick between the items loaded on a wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cart' is a verb here (carry), not a vehicle. The definition alludes to the saying 'beggars can't be choosers'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that a person living on charity is in no position to be choosy.

clue.text: In essence, a strong point

indicators.note: the answer lies in these words, its letters running across them

explanation.surface: Essentially, something counts as a strong argument.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'essencE A STrong'. 'Point' reads like a point in an argument but is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: East is one of the four cardinal points of the compass.

clue.text: Agents fail to spot sign on back of cape

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece on another comes after it
the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: to fail to spot something is to miss it
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Secret agents overlook a signal positioned behind a headland or cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' is a zodiac sign, and in an across answer 'on' puts what precedes it after what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Emissaries are envoys sent on a mission, so they act as agents for those who send them.

clue.text: King for example earns plenty, I suspect

indicators.note: suspect means doubtful or not to be trusted, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a monarch, say, makes a great deal of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King' seems to be royalty, but it is Billie Jean King, a Wimbledon champion; 'suspect' rearranges EARNS PLENTY I.
explanation.definitionFit: Billie Jean King won many Grand Slam titles, so she is an example of a professional sportswoman on court.

clue.text: Fell asleep, having bowed out

parts.note: to bow the head is to nod
off and out both mean away or not on

explanation.surface: Someone dozed off after taking a bow and leaving the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodded off is an idiom for drifting into sleep.

clue.text: Want to put mark on urban development

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
a city is a large urban settlement

explanation.surface: An instruction to deface a new town development.
explanation.definitionFit: Want here is a noun meaning lack, the same as scarcity.

clue.text: Get every one, after some time, to city in Florida

indicators.note: one piece placed after another follows it in the answer

parts.note: a day is a period of time
to get or seize someone is to nab them
each means every one

explanation.surface: Instructions to collect everyone and, after a while, travel to a Florida city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the getting and the every one behind the time and 'to', which is used as a letter piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Daytona Beach is a resort city on the Atlantic coast of Florida, known for its motor racing.

clue.text: Article penned by solver: end translated in African capital

indicators.note: something penned by another is enclosed within it

parts.note: the clue speaks to the solver as you
a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: translated means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An article written by the solver: its end rendered into another language in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned by' looks like writing, but it means enclosed; 'translated' rearranges 'end' into NDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Yaoundé is the capital city of Cameroon in west-central Africa.

clue.text: Alongside a river, monster eats

indicators.note: something that eats another takes it inside

parts.note: a beast is a monster

explanation.surface: Beside a river, a monstrous creature is feeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Abreast means side by side, level with something.

clue.text: Swan has key element

parts.note: a cob is a male swan
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A swan possesses a crucial ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' reads as essential but is a keyboard key.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobalt is a chemical element, a hard bluish metal.

clue.text: Composer, one carrying fuel to the audience?

indicators.note: what is meant for an audience is heard, so a word of the same sound but different spelling is wanted

parts.note: coal is a fuel
a porter is someone who carries luggage

explanation.surface: A musician is described as a deliverer of coal, as heard by listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: COAL said aloud gives COLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cole Porter was the American songwriter of 'Anything Goes' and 'Night and Day'.

clue.text: Awful leaders of dictatorships, in Roman emperors

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their opening letters, one from each word

explanation.surface: Dictatorships under the rule of Roman emperors were dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire and awful are synonyms, both meaning dreadful or extremely bad.

clue.text: Material extracted from below

indicators.note: in a down answer, read from below means bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: mined means dug out, extracted

explanation.surface: Fabric that has been dug up from under the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From below' reverses MINED in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing cotton twill cloth used for jeans.

clue.text: Forsake colour

definitions.meaning: to abandon them, as on a desert island

explanation.surface: Abandon a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to strand someone and a dark reddish-brown shade.

clue.text: Marine animal consuming rubbish is an edible mollusc

indicators.note: something consuming another takes it inside

parts.note: a seal is a marine mammal

indicators.note: rubbish describes the following letters as worthless, so they are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sea creature eats garbage, which is said to be an edible mollusc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marine animal' looks like the definition but is wordplay; 'rubbish' jumbles IS AN into SNAI, which goes inside the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea snails such as whelks and winkles are gastropods eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Middle of speech by beau, sweet

indicators.note: one piece by another sits beside it, here following

parts.note: a beau is a dandy, and toff is British slang for a well-dressed upper-class man

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter or letters

explanation.surface: A boyfriend delivers the central part of a lovely speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beau' suggests a boyfriend, but here it is a fop; the middle letters of 'speech' are EE.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffee is a chewy confection, a sweet in British usage (candy in American).

clue.text: Chunky mole holding in stomach

indicators.note: something holding another in contains it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a mole is an infiltrating spy
tum is informal for stomach

explanation.surface: A burrowing mole sucks in its belly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' looks like the animal but is a secret agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumpy describes something short and thick, which is what chunky means.
